topic.title: Uber did 4.1 billion rides and deliveries in three months: of the fare you pay, how much does Uber keep, and how much is left as its profit?

title: Your Uber fare splits in two. How much does Uber keep? 🚗
description:
Uber did billions of rides and deliveries in three months. So how much of the fare you pay does Uber actually keep?
Sources: Uber Q3 2026 results (Sep 2026). The characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.

Logo: Wolff Olins, in collaboration with Uber's Brand Team [1], Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Uber_logo_2018.svg)
cta: Driver or the app: who earns more from your ride? Comment

lines.text: Your Uber fare splits in two when you pay. How much stays with Uber?
And Uber does that 4.1B times in three months, rides and deliveries.
Rohan's ride home is the average trip: about $15.
Most of it goes on to the driver, or to the restaurant and the courier.
Uber keeps about 25% of it. So is that its profit?
No. It pays for insurance, servers, staff and ads.
What Uber has left at the end is just 2.3% of Rohan's fare.
Driver or app: who earns more? Check your fare.

notes: 18 figures computed from inputs; 18 cross-checked against closed-form formulas.

note: 1 beats between the hook and the payoff open a new question; at least 2 ("But that's not where the dealer makes his money.", "So why would he give it away?"): the viewer always waits for something

All 4 facts confirmed on the SEC 8-K Q3 2026 release (4 Nov 2026, latest): gross bookings $59,819M ($59.8B), trips 4,061M (4.1B), revenue $14,766M ($14.8B), GAAP income from operations $1,447M ($1.4B). Verify list met: 'rides and deliveries' said, per-trip figures framed as the average trip, no revenue comparison with earlier years. Lines about Uber's costs (insurance, servers, staff, ads) are accurate. Description ends with the disclaimer, no advice or expert framing. Notes: 2.3% is operating profit (net income was $512M, ~0.9%), so 'left at the end' means after running costs; gross bookings include $1.77B of Freight, so the $15 'average trip' is a whole-company average (~$14.3 without Freight, still 'about').
